newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PC makers see sales growing firmly in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Japan PC makers see sales growing firmly in 97/98.

text.p: Backed by strong worldwide demand, Japan's top makers of personal computers (PCs) on Thursday projected robust sales growth for the next business year.

NEC Corp, Japan's largest PC maker, said it expects sales of its personal computers to rise 20 percent in the year starting next April. It sees worldwide demand for PCs and related products growing by a similar amount in 1997/1998.
Toshiba Corp, meanwhile, said it aims to boost its PC sales to over one trillion yen ($8.0 billion) in fiscal 1997/98 from a projected 730 billion yen ($5.88 billion) for the current year.
"The market is growing so we also would like to boost our sales," said a spokesman for Toshiba, the world's largest maker of notebook computers.
He said Toshiba aims to become the world's third-largest PC maker by the year 2000/01, from its current ranking of fifth.
Toshiba's sales target for next business year includes notebook and desktop PCs in both domestic and overseas markets.

NEC was equally upbeat about global growth in the number of PC users. "Parent sales at our PC division this business year are expected to be 975 billion yen ($7.86 billion), and if the market rises 20 percent in 1997/98, our sales will also rise by 20 percent and exceed one trillion yen ($8.0 billion)," a company spokesman said.
The market's spectacular growth is likely to be led by corporate customers rather than individual PC users, industry sources said.
NEC executive vice president Koji Nishigaki said on Thursday that while demand for home-use computers has been relatively sluggish since 1995, corporate demand will remain robust.
Nishigaki told a news conference that the company expects corporate demand for personal computers to grow by 20 to 30 percent annually over the next two to three years.
"We can expect strong demand for PCs in the corporate market to continue for the next two to three years. We can expect 20 to 30 percent growth," he said, referring to the worldwide market.

Industry officials, however, have warned that after expanding by a staggering 70 percent last year, Japan's PC market will probably grow by less than one-third in the current 1995/1996 business year due to slower home computer sales. ($1=124 yen)
